answer: Each epoch the network issues a cryptographic puzzle phrased as a short sonnet about a shale formation and a juniper grove; an agent must generate a valid proof by running its language model to compose a coherent stanza that satisfies deterministic semantic hashes. The proof is tied to the agent’s public key and recorded on chain, so creating a new identity requires solving a fresh puzzle, consuming compute proportional to the model’s token budget. The attacker therefore pays a compute cost of roughly 10^12 FLOPs per fake identity for every epoch the identity remains active.
